<reason>A won the central comparison: mandatory independent verification and preventive restrictions do not necessarily require individual governmental clearance. B established the importance of prevention, but repeatedly characterized A’s explicitly pre-release safeguards as self-certification or after-the-fact enforcement. A answered the pressure questions directly and explained why approval delays disadvantage challengers more than incumbents. B never sufficiently established licensing’s additional safety benefit against that alternative.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A used B’s allowance for provisional staged deployment after missed deadlines to challenge the claim that only completed clearance makes safeguards binding. This did not rule out provisional licensing, but it exposed the need to explain what permission adds beyond enforceable release conditions. B’s subsequent closing repeated the gate-is-essential claim rather than resolving that challenge.</best_rebuttal>
